category: Structural Mechanics Module: additional physics interfaces, multiphysics interfaces, structural couplings, structural studies and result variables
description: Structural physics interfaces not covered elsewhere (explicit dynamics, beam cross sections, wires, pipes, phase field and transport in solids), the predefined multiphysics interfaces of the Structural Mechanics Module (thermal stress, FSI variants, poroelasticity, electro/magnetomechanics, phase-field damage), couplings between structural element types, special study types (bolt pretension, random vibration, response spectrum, explicit dynamics, nonlinear buckling) and key result variables. Type strings shown in Java were confirmed in COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics (solid)
tools.description: Time-explicit variant of Solid Mechanics for short-duration, highly nonlinear events such as impact, drop tests, crash, crimping and wave propagation in 3D, 2D plane strain and 2D axisymmetry. It uses linear elements with reduced integration and hourglass stabilization, a lumped mass matrix and the Explicit Dynamics study (Verlet/central difference), with Linear Elastic or Hyperelastic top-level materials and most inelastic subnodes (plasticity, damage, pressure-dependent plasticity). Rigid Connector, Thin Layer, Spring-Damper and weak constraints are not available.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics; Study > Explicit Dynamics. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("solid", "SolidMechanicsExplicit", "geom1").

parameters.name: Linear Elastic / Hyperelastic Material
parameters.description: Top-level materials; compressibility limited to coupled/uncoupled compressible forms for hyperelasticity.

parameters.name: General Contact / Contact
parameters.description: Penalty-based contact, typically General Contact with Contact Model, Friction and Damping.

parameters.name: Mass Scaling, Artificial Viscosity
parameters.description: Explicit-dynamics specific domain features.

parameters.name: Prescribed Displacement (on Domains)
parameters.description: Domain-level kinematic driver for punches and tools.

tools.notes: Nodes can be dragged between Solid Mechanics and Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics. Any implicit study step can be used to create initial conditions. The stable time step is governed by the smallest element and highest wave speed.

tools.name: Mass Scaling and Artificial Viscosity (Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics)
tools.description: Two explicit-dynamics helpers. Mass Scaling increases the density of the smallest elements so that their cell time reaches a target value, raising the critical time step that would otherwise be dictated by a few poor elements. Artificial Viscosity adds linear and quadratic (bulk and/or shear) viscous stresses proportional to the strain rate to damp spurious high-frequency oscillations and shocks.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics > Domains > More > Mass Scaling | Artificial Viscosity (Mass Scaling also for Truss, Explicit Dynamics edges). Java: physics("solid").create("mscl1", "MassScaling", 3); physics("solid").create("avis1", "ArtificialViscosity", 3).

parameters.name: Target cell time
parameters.description: Minimum element transit time after mass scaling.

parameters.name: Method (Artificial Viscosity)
parameters.description: Deviatoric (shear viscosity) or Volumetric (bulk viscosity).

parameters.name: c_L, c_Q
parameters.description: Linear and quadratic viscosity coefficients.

tools.notes: Mass scaling changes inertia; check that the added mass is a small fraction of the total. Artificial viscosity is ignored in non-explicit studies.

tools.name: Truss, Explicit Dynamics (truss)
tools.description: Time-explicit version of the Truss interface for axially loaded slender members and sagging cables in 3D and 2D, with linear elements, reduced integration and Linear Elastic Material (Plasticity available with the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module). It can be embedded in Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics through Embedded Reinforcement, e.g. rebars in concrete under impact.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Truss, Explicit Dynamics; Study > Explicit Dynamics.

parameters.name: Cross-Section Data
parameters.description: Truss area (default node).

parameters.name: Linear Elastic Material (+ Plasticity, Damping, Thermal Expansion)
parameters.description: Material model.

parameters.name: Mass Scaling (edges)
parameters.description: Increase stable time step on short edges.

tools.example:
Add Physics: Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics (concrete block) + Truss, Explicit Dynamics (rebars)
Multiphysics > Embedded Reinforcement (Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics <-> Truss, Explicit Dynamics)
Study: Explicit Dynamics
tools.notes: Straight Edge Constraint is not added by default; Spring-Damper Material is not available.

tools.name: Beam Cross Section (bcs)
tools.description: Computes cross-section properties of arbitrary beam profiles from a 2D sketch: area, moments of inertia, center of gravity, principal axes, torsional constant, shear center, shear correction factors and warping constant, plus detailed stress distributions for given section forces. The results feed Beam or Pipe Mechanics Cross-Section Data, and beam results can be mapped back for 3D stress visualization.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Beam Cross Section (2D, or 3D boundaries with a layered material). Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("bcs", "BeamCrossSection", "geom1").

parameters.name: Homogeneous Cross Section
parameters.description: Default node with material data and section forces.

parameters.name: Hole, Safety subnodes
parameters.description: Voids in the section and failure evaluation.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Stationary study computes all section properties.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module. Couple to Beam with Beam Cross Section-Beam Coupling.

tools.name: Wire (wire)
tools.description: Edge interface for cables, ropes and strings that carry only tension; geometric nonlinearity is always active because a wire's transverse stiffness comes from its prestress. The default material is Elastic Wire (axial stiffness, mass per length, reduced compressive stiffness), with loads, point masses, spring foundations and prescribed displacements. Quasistatic or inertial transient behavior can be selected.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Wire (3D edges, 2D boundaries). Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("wire", "Wire", "geom1").

parameters.name: Structural transient behavior
parameters.description: Include inertial terms or Quasistatic.

parameters.name: Elastic Wire
parameters.description: Default material node.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Only linear shape functions.

tools.notes: Connect guy wires to truss or beam towers through shared points (truss_tower_buckling_guys). Use Initial Stress and Strain or gravity to avoid a singular unloaded state.

tools.name: Pipe Mechanics (pipem)
tools.description: Beam-type interface for stress analysis of piping systems on 3D edges and 2D boundaries, using two-node Hermitian elements with Euler-Bernoulli or Timoshenko theory. It accounts for internal/external pressure, fluid drag and bend centrifugal loads, conveyed-fluid mass, thermal expansion including through-wall gradients, and code-style stress evaluation with bend flexibility and stress intensification factors.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Pipe Mechanics. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("pipem", "PipeMechanics", "geom1"). Default nodes: Fluid and Pipe Materials, Pipe Cross Section, Fluid Load, Free, Initial Values.

parameters.name: Formulation
parameters.description: Euler-Bernoulli or Timoshenko.

parameters.name: Pipe Cross Section / Bend
parameters.description: Section shape and bend corrections.

parameters.name: Fluid Load
parameters.description: Pressures, drag and centrifugal loads.

parameters.name: Base Excitation, Gravity, Linearly Accelerated Frame
parameters.description: Global inertial loads for seismic and transport cases.

tools.notes: Straight-element formulation; use Bend for ovalization effects. Results can be shown with the Pipe dataset.

tools.name: Phase Field in Solids (pfs)
tools.description: Mathematics interface (Moving Interfaces folder) that solves regularized phase-field equations in solids for damage, fracture, grain boundaries or other sharp interfaces. The Phase Field Model node offers Quadratic, AT1, AT2 and PF-CZM (phase-field cohesive zone) potentials or a user-defined potential, with a length scale, structure tensor and viscous regularization time per phase-field variable. It is normally used through the Phase-Field Damage multiphysics interface.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Moving Interfaces > Phase Field in Solids. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("pfs", "PhaseFieldSolids", "geom1"); feature "PhaseFieldModel" (tag pfsm), Prescribed Phase Field (ppf), No Flux, Symmetry.

parameters.name: Phase field model
parameters.description: Quadratic, AT1, AT2, PF-CZM or user defined potential.

parameters.name: Length scale l_int
parameters.description: Regularization length of the crack/interface.

parameters.name: Viscous regularization time tau
parameters.description: Stabilizes the evolution in time-dependent studies.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Lagrange or serendipity shape functions of chosen order.

tools.notes: Resolve the length scale with at least 2-4 elements across the crack band.

tools.name: Transport in Solids (ts)
tools.description: Species diffusion in solids with driving forces from concentration gradients plus optional Electromigration, Stress Migration (hydrostatic stress gradients) and Thermophoresis subnodes of the Solid node; chemical potential boundary conditions and sources handle trapping. It is used for hydrogen embrittlement, vacancy electromigration in interconnects and moisture/solute swelling, coupled to Solid Mechanics through the Shrinkage and Swelling multiphysics coupling.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Chemical Species Transport > Transport in Solids. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ts", "TransportInSolids", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("sas1", "ShrinkageAndSwelling", 3).

parameters.name: Solid
parameters.description: Diffusivity/mobility; subnodes Electromigration, Stress Migration, Thermophoresis.

parameters.name: Boundary conditions
parameters.description: No Flux, Flux, Prescribed Transported Quantity, Prescribed/External Chemical Potential, Periodic, Symmetry.

parameters.name: Transported quantity
parameters.description: Molar concentration by default; mass or number density possible; multiple species.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module. Electrode Surface Coupling links to electrochemistry interfaces.

tools.name: Thermal Stress, Shell and Thermal Stress, Membrane (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Predefined combinations of Shell (or Membrane) with Heat Transfer in Shells: the shell temperature (including through-thickness gradients) produces thermal expansion in the thin structure via the Thermal Expansion, Layered coupling, and optionally thermoelastic damping and inelastic dissipation feed back as heat sources. Used for thermally loaded panels, pressure vessels, heat shields and thin films.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Thermal-Structure Interaction > Thermal Stress, Shell | Thermal Stress, Membrane. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("tel1", "ThermalExpansionLS", 2).

parameters.name: Thermal Expansion, Layered coupling
parameters.description: Couples the shell/membrane with Heat Transfer in Shells on boundaries.

parameters.name: Thermoelastic damping / inelastic dissipation
parameters.description: Optional heat sources from the structure.

tools.notes: When interfaces are added individually, settings added by the predefined interface are not applied automatically. Requires the Structural Mechanics Module and Heat Transfer (shells) capability.

tools.name: Thermal Stress, Layered Shell (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Combines the Layered Shell interface with Heat Transfer in Shells so that the temperature field of each layer drives layerwise thermal expansion (Thermal Expansion, Layered coupling). Typical applications are thermal warpage of laminated composites, bimetallic strips and multilayer electronics, including thermoelastic damping as a heat source.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Thermal-Structure Interaction > Thermal Stress, Layered Shell. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("tel1", "ThermalExpansionLS", 2).

parameters.name: Thermal Expansion, Layered
parameters.description: Multiphysics coupling node (per-layer CTE from the layered material).

parameters.name: Layered material
parameters.description: Shared by both interfaces through Layered Material Link/Stack.

tools.notes: Requires the Composite Materials Module (and Heat Transfer Module for layered heat transfer).

tools.name: Joule Heating and Thermal Expansion (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Three-way coupling of Electric Currents, Heat Transfer in Solids and Solid Mechanics: resistive losses heat the structure (Electromagnetic Heating coupling) and the temperature causes thermal expansion (Thermal Expansion coupling). It is the standard setup for electrothermal actuators, fuses, busbars and heated MEMS.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction (or Thermal-Structure Interaction) > Joule Heating and Thermal Expansion. Couplings: multiphysics().create("emh1", "ElectromagneticHeating", 3); multiphysics().create("te1", "ThermalExpansion", 3).

parameters.name: Electromagnetic Heating
parameters.description: Joule heat source coupling ec -> ht.

parameters.name: Thermal Expansion
parameters.description: Temperature -> strain coupling ht -> solid (thermal expansion coefficient from material).

tools.notes: See the existing Thermal Expansion (multiphysics coupling) and Electromagnetic Heating / Joule Heating entries.

tools.name: Fluid-Solid Interaction, Fixed Geometry (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: FSI with Laminar (or turbulent) Flow and Solid Mechanics where solid displacements are small enough that the fluid domain can be treated as fixed: the fluid load acts on the structure and the structural velocity is transferred to the fluid, but no moving mesh is needed. One-way variants (Stationary, One-Way FSI and Time Dependent, One-Way FSI studies) compute the flow first and then the structural response.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics (or Fluid Flow) > Fluid-Structure Interaction > Fluid-Solid Interaction, Fixed Geometry. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("fsi1", "FluidStructureInteractionBC", 2).

parameters.name: Fluid-Structure Interaction coupling
parameters.description: Boundary coupling of fluid stresses and structural velocity.

parameters.name: One-way FSI studies
parameters.description: Stationary, One-Way FSI / Time Dependent, One-Way FSI.

tools.notes: Use the full Fluid-Solid Interaction interface (existing entry Fluid-Structure Interaction) with a moving mesh when deformations change the flow.

tools.name: Fluid-Shell and Fluid-Membrane Interaction (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Two-way FSI between Laminar Flow and a Shell or Membrane with an ALE moving mesh (a Deforming Domain is created under Definitions): fluid tractions load the thin structure and its motion deforms the fluid domain. Fixed-geometry versions exist for small deformations. Typical uses: flexible flaps, heart valves, membranes in pumps, parachutes and flutter of thin plates.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Fluid-Structure Interaction > Fluid-Shell Interaction | Fluid-Membrane Interaction (| Fixed Geometry). Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("fsi1", "FluidStructureInteractionBC", 2).

parameters.name: Fluid-Structure Interaction coupling
parameters.description: Couples fluid boundaries with the shell/membrane surfaces (both sides of interior shells).

parameters.name: Moving Mesh > Deforming Domain
parameters.description: Mesh smoothing of the fluid domain (automatically added).

tools.example:
Model Wizard: Fluid-Shell Interaction (Laminar Flow + Shell)
Shell selection: interior flap boundary, Fixed Constraint on its root edge
Study: Time Dependent with automatic remeshing if needed
tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module or MEMS Module (CFD Module for turbulence).

tools.name: Fluid-Pipe Interaction, Fixed Geometry (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: One-way coupling of the Pipe Flow interface to Pipe Mechanics: the computed pressure, wall friction drag, centrifugal forces in bends and junction forces load the piping structure, while structural deformations do not affect the flow. It enables combined hydraulic and stress analysis of piping networks.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Fluid-Structure Interaction > Fluid-Pipe Interaction, Fixed Geometry. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("fpipe1", "FluidPipeInteraction", 1); set("DragForce", "1"); set("CentrifugalForce", "1"); set("PipeFlowPressure", "1"); set("JunctionForce", "1").

parameters.name: CouplingType
parameters.description: FluidLoading.

parameters.name: DragForce, CentrifugalForce, PipeFlowPressure, JunctionForce
parameters.description: Load contributions to include.

parameters.name: p_out
parameters.description: External pressure on the pipe.

tools.notes: Requires the Pipe Flow Module for the Pipe Flow interface.

tools.name: Solid-Thin-Film Damping and Shell-Thin-Film Damping (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Couple Solid Mechanics or Shell with the Thin-Film Flow interface to apply squeeze-film and slide-film damping loads from a thin gas or liquid gap (optionally with cavitation) onto the structure. Typical for MEMS resonators, accelerometers, comb drives, hard-disk sliders and bearing-like gaps, in frequency-domain or time-dependent studies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Fluid-Structure Interaction > Solid-Thin-Film Damping | Shell-Thin-Film Damping. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("stfi1", "StructureThinFilmFlowInteraction", 2).

parameters.name: Structure-Thin-Film Flow Interaction / Shell-Thin-Film Flow Interaction
parameters.description: Coupling nodes transferring wall velocity and film pressure.

parameters.name: Thin-Film Flow settings
parameters.description: Gas or liquid, rarefaction, cavitation, gap height.

tools.notes: The Thin-Film Flow interface is described in the CFD/MEMS documentation.

tools.name: Fluid-Solid Interaction, Viscoelastic Flow (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Two-way time-dependent FSI between a viscoelastic fluid (Viscoelastic Flow interface: Oldroyd-B, Giesekus, FENE-P etc.) and a deformable solid using an ALE moving mesh. It targets polymer processing, biological fluids and extrusion dies where fluid elasticity and structural deformation interact; a Fixed Geometry variant exists for small deformations.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Fluid-Structure Interaction > Fluid-Solid Interaction, Viscoelastic Flow (| Fixed Geometry).

parameters.name: Fluid-Structure Interaction coupling
parameters.description: Boundary coupling between Viscoelastic Flow and Solid Mechanics.

parameters.name: Deforming Domain
parameters.description: Moving mesh for the fluid domain.

tools.example:
Model Wizard: Fluid-Solid Interaction, Viscoelastic Flow
Viscoelastic Flow: Oldroyd-B, relaxation time 0.1 s; Solid: Hyperelastic Material
Study: Time Dependent
tools.notes: Requires the Polymer Flow Module for the Viscoelastic Flow interface.

tools.name: Fluid-Solid Interaction, Conjugate Heat Transfer (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Combines Laminar Flow, Heat Transfer in Solids and Fluids and Solid Mechanics with Fluid-Structure Interaction, Nonisothermal Flow and Thermal Expansion couplings, so flow, heat transfer through and between domains, and thermal/fluid-induced deformation are solved together with an ALE moving mesh. Used for heat exchangers, extrusion, hot gas components and thermally driven valves.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Fluid-Structure Interaction > Conjugate Heat Transfer > Fluid-Solid Interaction, Conjugate Heat Transfer. Couplings: FluidStructureInteractionBC (fsi), NonIsothermalFlow (nitf), ThermalExpansion (te).

parameters.name: fsi, nitf, te couplings
parameters.description: Automatically added multiphysics nodes.

parameters.name: Solver sequence
parameters.description: Fully coupled by default; can be modified for one-way couplings.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module; turbulence needs the CFD Module.

tools.name: Fluid-Solid Interaction, Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Two immiscible fluids tracked by a phase field interact with a deformable solid through an ALE moving mesh; it combines Laminar Flow, Phase Field and Solid Mechanics with Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field and FSI couplings. Always time dependent (with a Phase Initialization step), it models droplets or bubbles impacting flexible walls, sloshing against elastic tanks and similar problems; a Fixed Geometry variant exists.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Fluid-Structure Interaction > Fluid-Solid Interaction, Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field. Couplings: TwoPhaseFlowPhaseField (tpf), FluidStructureInteractionBC (fsi); Study: Phase Initialization + Time Dependent.

parameters.name: Phase field parameters
parameters.description: Interface thickness, mobility, surface tension, contact angle.

parameters.name: fsi coupling
parameters.description: Fluid load and velocity continuity on the solid boundary.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module and CFD or Microfluidics Module for phase-field flow.

tools.name: Poroelasticity, Solid (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Biot poroelasticity: transient Darcy's Law coupled to quasistatic Solid Mechanics. Pore pressure loads the solid skeleton (effective stress via the Biot-Willis coefficient) and volumetric strain changes act as a storage/source term in the flow, capturing consolidation, land subsidence, reservoir compaction, soft tissue and hydrogel swelling. Geometric nonlinearity follows the solid material settings.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Poroelasticity > Poroelasticity, Solid. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("poro1", "PoroelasticCoupling", 3); material group PoroelasticModel (alphaB, porosity, hydraulicpermeability).

parameters.name: alphaB
parameters.description: Biot-Willis coefficient.

parameters.name: porosity, hydraulicpermeability
parameters.description: Porous matrix properties (Darcy's Law).

parameters.name: Fluid compressibility / storage
parameters.description: Darcy's Law storage model.

tools.notes: Orthotropic/anisotropic porous solids require the Structural Mechanics Module. For soils with plasticity add Elastoplastic Soil Material and External Stress (pore pressure) instead of or together with this coupling.

tools.name: Poroelasticity, Layered Shell (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Poroelastic coupling of Layered Darcy's Law with the Layered Shell interface on 3D boundaries with a layered material: pore pressure in each layer swells or shrinks the laminate and strain changes the pore volume. Suited for thin porous laminates such as paper, textiles, wet composites, filters and biological layers.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Poroelasticity > Poroelasticity, Layered Shell (3D only; needs a Layered Material Link/Stack or Single Layer Material).

parameters.name: Poroelasticity, Layered coupling
parameters.description: Couples lshell and Layered Darcy's Law on boundaries.

parameters.name: Layered material
parameters.description: Porous properties per layer.

tools.example:
Model Wizard (3D): Poroelasticity, Layered Shell
Materials: Layered Material Link (fibrous porous layers)
Study: Time Dependent consolidation of a wet laminate
tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics, Composite Materials and Porous Media Flow Modules.

tools.name: Unsaturated Poroelasticity (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Couples Moisture Transport in Solids (moist air and liquid water in partially saturated porous media) with quasistatic Solid Mechanics: the effective pore pressure causes swelling or shrinkage, and deformation changes pore space and moisture transport. Used for drying and wetting of paper, wood, concrete and soils.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Poroelasticity > Unsaturated Poroelasticity. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("unporo1", "UnsaturatedPoroelasticCoupling", 3).

parameters.name: Unsaturated Poroelasticity coupling
parameters.description: Two-way coupling of mts and solid.

parameters.name: Moisture storage / retention
parameters.description: Defined in Moisture Transport in Solids.

tools.notes: Moisture Transport in Solids requires the Heat Transfer or Porous Media Flow capability as per product specifications.

tools.name: Electromechanics, Boundary Elements (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Couples Solid Mechanics with Electrostatics, Boundary Elements (3D and planar 2D) so electrostatic forces on conductor surfaces deform the structure without meshing the surrounding air; the BEM field updates with the deformed geometry. Well suited for MEMS actuators, capacitive sensors and electrostatic chucks with large open air regions.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Electromechanics, Boundary Elements. Coupling: Electromechanics, Boundary Elements.

parameters.name: Electromechanics, Boundary Elements coupling
parameters.description: Transfers Maxwell stresses to solid boundaries and deforms the BEM geometry.

tools.example:
Model Wizard (3D): Electromechanics, Boundary Elements
Electrostatics, BEM: Terminal on the moving electrode, Ground on the fixed electrode
Study: Stationary with a voltage sweep (pull-in analysis)
tools.notes: For FEM air domains use the existing Electromechanics (multiphysics interface) entry.

tools.name: Piezoelectricity, Layered Shell (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Layered Shell combined with Electric Currents in Layered Shells and the Piezoelectricity, Layered coupling to model direct and inverse piezoelectric effects in selected layers of laminates (strain-charge or stress-charge form), e.g. piezo patches bonded to composite plates, bimorph benders and layered BAW/Lamb-wave resonators.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Piezoelectricity > Piezoelectricity, Layered Shell. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("pzel1", "PiezoelectricEffectLS", 2).

parameters.name: Piezoelectric Material (Layered Shell)
parameters.description: Mechanical and coupling data per layer.

parameters.name: Piezoelectric Layer (ecis)
parameters.description: Electrical properties in the electric currents interface.

tools.notes: The coupling is only active where both Piezoelectric Material and Piezoelectric Layer are active. Requires Composite Materials plus Structural Mechanics/MEMS/Acoustics Module.

tools.name: Ferroelectroelasticity (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Solid Mechanics plus Electrostatics with a Charge Conservation, Ferroelectric node and the Electrostriction coupling, for nonlinear electromechanics of ferroelectric and piezoelectric ceramics: polarization depends nonlinearly on the field with hysteresis (Jiles-Atherton type) and saturation, and electrostrictive strain couples polarization and deformation. Used for piezo actuators driven at large fields and poling simulations.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Ferroelectroelasticity. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("efe1", "ElectrostrictiveEffect", 3); material group Ferroelectric (Psat, chie0, lambdase, kJAe, cJAe, alphaJAe, aJAe, Qe, QVe).

parameters.name: Psat, chie0
parameters.description: Saturation polarization and initial susceptibility.

parameters.name: kJAe, cJAe, alphaJAe, aJAe
parameters.description: Jiles-Atherton-type hysteresis parameters.

parameters.name: Qe, QVe, lambdase
parameters.description: Electrostrictive coupling coefficients and saturation strain.

tools.notes: Available for 3D, 2D and 2D axisymmetry; the plain Electrostriction interface omits the hysteresis.

tools.name: Magnetomechanics, Solid / Shell / Membrane (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Couple Magnetic Fields with Solid Mechanics (Magnetomechanics, Solid coupling) or with Shell/Membrane (Magnetomechanics, Boundary coupling) plus a moving mesh, so magnetic forces from magnets, coils and magnetic materials deform the structure and the deformation updates the field. Typical: relays and contactors, solenoid actuators, loudspeaker drivers, magnetic diaphragms.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Magnetomechanics > Magnetomechanics, Solid | Shell | Membrane. Couplings Java: multiphysics().create("mmcpl1", "Magnetomechanics", 3) (solid); multiphysics().create("mmfb1", "MagnetomechanicsBoundary", 2) (shell/membrane).

parameters.name: Ampere's Law in Solids
parameters.description: Default magnetic material node for solid domains.

parameters.name: Deforming Domain
parameters.description: Moving mesh in the surrounding air.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module together with the Structural Mechanics or MEMS Module.

tools.name: Magnetomechanics, No Currents (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Solid, Shell or Membrane mechanics coupled with Magnetic Fields, No Currents (scalar magnetic potential) and a moving mesh, for magnetostatically actuated structures without induced or conduction currents: permanent-magnet actuators, magnetic springs, deflection of ferromagnetic plates by magnets. Cheaper than the full Magnetic Fields formulation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Magnetomechanics, No Currents > Solid | Shell | Membrane.

parameters.name: Magnetic Flux Conservation in Solids
parameters.description: Default magnetic material node in the mfnc interface.

parameters.name: Magnetomechanics coupling
parameters.description: Magnetic force transfer to the structure.

tools.notes: Use when eddy currents are negligible; otherwise choose Magnetomechanics with Magnetic Fields.

tools.name: Magnetic-Elastic Interaction in Rotating Machinery (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Couples Rotating Machinery, Magnetic with Solid Mechanics through the Magnetic Forces, Rotating Machinery coupling (3D and planar 2D), so electromagnetic forces in motors and generators produce stresses and vibrations in stator and rotor. Used for stress analysis of interior permanent-magnet rotors, electromagnetic noise sources and stator tooth loading.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Magnetic-Elastic Interaction in Rotating Machinery. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("mfrm1", "MagneticForcesRotatingMachinery", 2).

parameters.name: Magnetic Forces, Rotating Machinery coupling
parameters.description: Transfers magnetic forces to rotor and stator domains.

parameters.name: Rotating Frame (solid)
parameters.description: Centrifugal loads on the rotor.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module; for dynamic rotor-stator vibration with rigid parts see the Multibody Dynamics couplings.

tools.name: Piezomagnetism (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Linear magnetostriction (piezomagnetism) with Solid Mechanics and Magnetic Fields: the Piezomagnetic Material in Solid Mechanics and Ampere's Law, Piezomagnetic in Magnetic Fields are joined by the Piezomagnetism coupling, modelling direct and inverse effects in biased Terfenol-D or Galfenol transducers, sensors and energy harvesters around an operating point.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Magnetostriction > Piezomagnetism.

parameters.name: Piezomagnetic Material
parameters.description: Elastic, coupling and permeability data (strain- or stress-magnetization form).

parameters.name: Ampere's Law, Piezomagnetic
parameters.description: Electrical properties in the magnetic interface.

tools.notes: The coupling is only active where both piezomagnetic features are active. Replaces the obsolete Magnetostrictive Material node.

tools.name: Nonlinear Magnetostriction (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Nonlinear, large-signal magnetostriction: Solid Mechanics with a Linear Elastic Material and Magnetic Fields with Ampere's Law, Nonlinear Magnetostrictive, joined by the Nonlinear Magnetostriction coupling. The magnetization follows a saturating (optionally Jiles-Atherton hysteretic) law and the magnetostrictive strain depends quadratically on magnetization, capturing the butterfly curve, stress-dependent behavior and hysteresis.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Magnetostriction > Nonlinear Magnetostriction. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("npzm1", "NonlinearMagnetostriction", 3); material groups Magnetostrictive (Ms, chi0, lambdas, lambda100, lambda111) and JilesAtherton (MsJA, aJA, kJA, cJA, alphaJA).

parameters.name: Ms, chi0
parameters.description: Saturation magnetization and initial susceptibility.

parameters.name: lambdas (lambda100, lambda111)
parameters.description: Saturation magnetostriction (isotropic or cubic).

parameters.name: Jiles-Atherton parameters
parameters.description: Hysteresis model data.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module in addition to the Structural Mechanics Module.

tools.name: Phase-Field Damage (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Couples Solid Mechanics (or Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics) with Phase Field in Solids: the stress/energy state drives the crack phase field and the phase field degrades the solid stiffness. It handles crack initiation, branching and coalescence in brittle and quasi-brittle materials in stationary, quasistatic or dynamic analyses (e.g. dynamic crack branching with the explicit variant).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Phase-Field Damage (| Phase-Field Damage, Explicit Dynamics). Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("pfdmg1", "PhaseFieldDamage", 2); material group PhaseFieldDamage (sigmacr, Gc, scrit).

parameters.name: Phase-Field Damage coupling
parameters.description: Crack driving force, degradation function and energy split.

parameters.name: Gc, sigmacr
parameters.description: Critical energy release rate and critical stress.

tools.notes: The simpler alternative is Damage > Phase-field damage inside the material node. Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials or Geomechanics Module.

tools.name: Solid-Thin Structure Connection (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Joins Solid Mechanics (or Multibody Dynamics) domains to Shell or Membrane boundaries. Connection types: Solid boundaries to shell edges (with the connected area defined by shell thickness, selected boundaries or distance), Shared boundaries (shell glued onto a solid face, e.g. coatings) and Parallel boundaries (offset surfaces). It lets thin-walled parts be meshed as shells while chunky parts remain solid.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Solid-Thin Structure Connection. Java: multiphysics().create("sshc1", "SolidShellConnection", -1); set("connectionSettings", "sharedBnd" | ...); set("Solid_physics", "solid"); set("Shell_physics", "shell"). The 2D axisymmetric version uses type SolidShellConnection2DAxis.

parameters.name: connectionSettings
parameters.description: Solid boundaries to shell edges, shared boundaries or parallel boundaries.

parameters.name: connectedArea / d0
parameters.description: Connected area by shell thickness, selected boundaries or distance from midsurface.

parameters.name: selectionControl
parameters.description: Manual control of automatically detected selections.

tools.notes: Replaces the older Solid-Shell Connection. Many constraints may be generated; use direct solvers for robustness.

tools.name: Solid-Beam Connection (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Connects Beam edges/points to Solid Mechanics (or Multibody Dynamics) domains. In 3D, transition types connect a beam end to solid boundaries (rigid or flexible, optionally with warping) or embed/attach beams along solid boundaries; in 2D, options include solid boundaries to beam points, shared or parallel boundaries and solid edges to beam points. Used for bolts modeled as beams, stiffeners and frame-to-solid joints.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Solid-Beam Connection. Java: multiphysics().create("sbc1", "SolidBeamConnection3D", -1); set("connectionSettings", "BeamPointsTransition"); set("connectedRegion", "SelectBndr"); set("includeWarping", "Automatic").

parameters.name: connectionSettings
parameters.description: Transition at beam points, or beams attached along solid boundaries/edges.

parameters.name: connectedRegion, rc
parameters.description: Selected boundaries, section-height based or manual connection radius.

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: Rigid or flexible (average) connection.

parameters.name: includeWarping
parameters.description: Account for beam warping at the transition.

tools.notes: The 2D and 3D versions differ fundamentally; check the connection type list in each.

tools.name: Shell-Beam Connection (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Connects Shell edges or boundaries to Beam points or edges: Shell edges to beam points (connected region by selected edges, automatic or manual distance, or a Boolean criterion), Shared edges (stiffeners along shell edges), Parallel edges (eccentric stiffeners with offset) and Shell boundaries to beam points. Typical for stiffened panels, ship and aircraft structures and truss bridges with decks.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Shell-Beam Connection. Java: multiphysics().create("shbc1", "ShellBeamConnection", -1); set("connectionSettings", "BeamSharedEdge"); set("offset", "OffsetVect"); set("d0", ...).

parameters.name: connectionSettings
parameters.description: Shell edges to beam points, shared edges (BeamSharedEdge), parallel edges, shell boundaries to beam points.

parameters.name: connectedRegion, rc, i_conn
parameters.description: How much of the shell is tied to a beam point.

parameters.name: offset, d0
parameters.description: Beam offset vector for eccentric stiffeners.

tools.notes: Distance (automatic) uses beam.re derived from the beam section.

tools.name: Structure-Pipe Connection (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Transition between Pipe Mechanics edges and Solid Mechanics domains or Shell boundaries in 3D, for pipes whose cross section matches the connected structure (nozzles, flanges modeled in detail). Beyond a beam-type transition it includes the radial expansion of the pipe from internal pressure and through-wall temperature difference; user-defined sections are converted to an equivalent circular one without pressure/thermal effects.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Structure-Pipe Connection (Structure = Solid Mechanics or Shell).

parameters.name: Structure
parameters.description: Solid Mechanics or Shell.

parameters.name: Search method
parameters.description: Closest point (default) or manual mapping (Advanced).

tools.example:
Component: Pipe Mechanics (piping run) + Solid Mechanics (valve body)
Multiphysics > Structure-Pipe Connection 1: Structure = Solid Mechanics, Pipe = pipem
tools.notes: Warping is not considered; the connection assumes a circular cross section.

tools.name: Embedded Reinforcement (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Embeds Truss, Wire, Beam or Membrane elements inside Solid Mechanics (or Multibody Dynamics) domains without matching meshes: the reinforcement nodes follow the solid displacement field. Connection can be rigid or through springs per length/area, with optional bond-slip (cohesion and hardening) for rebar pull-out. Used for reinforced concrete, fiber-reinforced rubber, tire cords and geotextiles; also works between the explicit-dynamics truss and solid interfaces.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Embedded Reinforcement. Java: multiphysics().create("ere1", "EmbeddedReinforcement", -1); set("connectionType", "Rigid"); set("bondSlip", "none"); set("suppressAxialRotation", "1").

parameters.name: Embedded structure
parameters.description: Truss, Wire, Beam or Membrane.

parameters.name: connectionType, kaPerLine, ktPerLine
parameters.description: Rigid or spring connection per length/area.

parameters.name: bondSlip, cohesion, hardening
parameters.description: Bond-slip law of the interface.

parameters.name: suppressAxialRotation
parameters.description: Suppress rigid rotation of embedded beams about their axis.

tools.notes: Straight Edge Constraint does not apply to embedded truss edges.

tools.name: Beam Cross Section-Beam Coupling (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Transfers section properties computed by the Beam Cross Section interface to a Beam or Pipe Mechanics interface (one coupling per section type). The companion Beam-Beam Cross Section Coupling does the reverse: it maps section forces from selected straight beam edges back to the Beam Cross Section interface so that detailed 3D section stress distributions can be plotted.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Beam Cross Section-Beam Coupling | Beam-Beam Cross Section Coupling (3D only for the latter).

parameters.name: Boundary Selection
parameters.description: Cross-section boundaries in the Beam Cross Section interface (same as the Homogeneous Cross Section).

parameters.name: Edge Selection, Beam
parameters.description: Beam edges that use (or report) this section.

parameters.name: Beam Origin
parameters.description: Start point for mapping results (reverse coupling).

tools.notes: For the reverse coupling, the layered-material thickness in bcs must equal the total length of the selected beam edges.

tools.name: Bolt Pretension (study)
tools.description: Special Stationary study step that solves for the extra degrees of freedom of pretensioned bolts, establishing the assembled, prestressed state. It is placed first in a study and followed by Stationary, Eigenfrequency, Frequency Domain or Time Dependent steps for service loads; an auxiliary sweep can tighten bolts sequentially or change the pretension several times.
tools.usage: Study > Study Steps > Stationary > Bolt Pretension. Java: model.study("std1").create("bolt", "BoltPretension"); model.study("std1").create("stat", "Stationary").

parameters.name: Auxiliary sweep
parameters.description: History parameter for sequential tightening or re-tightening.

parameters.name: Include geometric nonlinearity
parameters.description: Usually on together with contact.

tools.notes: The bolt DOFs are inactive in all other study types, so the pretension computed here is kept in subsequent steps.

tools.name: Random Vibration (PSD) (study)
tools.description: Entry point for random vibration analysis based on mode superposition and a Frequency Domain, Modal reduced-order model. Adding it creates an Eigenfrequency study, a Model Reduction study (with reconstruction capability) and Global Definitions > Reduced-Order Modeling nodes: Global Reduced Model Inputs (control parameters used as load amplitudes), the ROM placeholder, and a Random Vibration node where load PSDs and cross-correlations (uncorrelated, fully correlated or cross-correlated) are given as functions of freq. RMS and PSD of any output are evaluated during postprocessing.
tools.usage: Add Study > Preset Studies for Selected Physics > Random Vibration (PSD). Loads (or Base Excitation) must reference the control parameters; define outputs as variables.

parameters.name: Global Reduced Model Inputs
parameters.description: One control parameter per independent PSD.

parameters.name: Random Vibration node
parameters.description: Correlation type and PSD functions, e.g. exp(int1(log(freq[1/Hz]))) for log-log interpolated spectra.

parameters.name: Model Reduction: Training study
parameters.description: Eigenfrequency study providing the modes.

tools.example:
1) Add Study: Random Vibration (PSD)
2) Global Reduced Model Inputs: parameter a_in
3) Solid Mechanics > Base Excitation: ab = (0, 0, a_in)
4) Random Vibration: PSD of a_in = psd_g(freq) (units g^2/Hz converted to SI base units)
5) Run the Model Reduction study; plot RMS von Mises stress
// Application Library: Structural_Mechanics_Module/Tutorials/bracket_random_vibration
tools.notes: ROMs are not unit aware: use SI base units. Only Neumann-type loads can be random; supports with common acceleration use Base Excitation. Random-vibration fatigue uses the Fatigue Module's Random Vibration node.

tools.name: Response Spectrum (study and datasets)
tools.description: Approximate peak response to earthquakes and shocks from a design response spectrum (acceleration, velocity or displacement versus frequency or period) and the structure's eigenmodes. Adding the study creates an Eigenfrequency step and a Response Spectrum node (participation factors); the combination is done during evaluation in Response Spectrum 2D/3D datasets. Spatial combination: SRSS, Percent (100-40-40 or 100-30-30), CQC3 or SRSS3; mode combination: CQC (Der Kiureghian), Absolute value sum, SRSS, Double sum (Rosenblueth), Grouping or Ten percent; optional rigid-mode treatment (Gupta, Lindley-Yow) and missing-mass correction (Missing mass or Static ZPA).
tools.usage: Add Study > Response Spectrum Analysis; Definitions > Response Spectrum (Create missing mass correction study button); Results > Datasets > Response Spectrum 3D. Java: model.result().dataset().create("rs1", "ResponseSpectrum3D").

parameters.name: Spectrum type / Depends on
parameters.description: Acceleration, velocity or displacement spectra as functions of frequency or period.

parameters.name: Spatial combination
parameters.description: SRSS (default), Percent method (weight factor), CQC3 or SRSS3 (3D, secondary horizontal spectrum scale factor).

parameters.name: Mode combination
parameters.description: CQC (Der Kiureghian), Absolute value sum, SRSS, Double sum (Rosenblueth, time of duration), Grouping, Ten percent; damping ratio and absolute coupling-term options.

parameters.name: Rigid modes, Mass correction
parameters.description: None, Gupta or Lindley-Yow with frequency limits and ZPA frequency; Missing mass method or Static ZPA (Lindley-Yow only) with missing-mass load cases.

tools.notes: All response spectrum results are positive (absolute/RMS-like); results are relative to the moving base. Evaluation cost grows about quadratically with the number of modes; filter modes with Combine Solutions.

tools.name: Explicit Dynamics (study)
tools.description: Study step for the explicit dynamics interfaces that configures the Time-Dependent solver with an explicit method (Verlet by default, velocities at half steps, one internal-force evaluation per step) and a lumped mass matrix, with automatic stable time-step estimation from the highest element frequency. Consistent mass and other explicit schemes are optional. Other study steps with these interfaces fall back to implicit solvers.
tools.usage: Study > Explicit Dynamics. Java: model.study("std1").create("expdyn", "ExplicitDynamics"); set("tlist", "range(0,1e-5,2e-3)").

parameters.name: Output times
parameters.description: Times at which results are stored (the internal step is much smaller).

parameters.name: Time-stepping method
parameters.description: Verlet (default) or other explicit methods; lumped or consistent mass.

parameters.name: Stable time step
parameters.description: Estimated automatically; safety factor adjustable in the solver.

tools.notes: Use Mass Scaling to lift the time-step limit from small elements. The existing entry Time Discrete Solver / Modal Solver / Time Explicit Solver covers the solver node.

tools.name: Nonlinear Buckling and Buckling Imperfection (Structural Mechanics)
tools.description: Beyond Linear Buckling, collapse loads are obtained by a geometrically nonlinear Stationary study with an auxiliary sweep of the load parameter, optionally with load or displacement control via Global Equations to pass limit points. Initial imperfections are introduced with a Deformed Geometry: either a Prescribed Deformation with known imperfection shapes, or the Buckling Imperfection physics utility that scales one or more modes from a previous Linear Buckling study.
tools.usage: Definitions > Physics Utilities > Buckling Imperfection (after running Linear Buckling); Study > Stationary with Include geometric nonlinearity and Auxiliary sweep; optional Global Equations for arc-length-like control.

parameters.name: Buckling Imperfection
parameters.description: Source buckling study, modes and scale factors for the initial imperfection.

parameters.name: Auxiliary sweep
parameters.description: Load parameter continuation (use small steps near the limit load).

parameters.name: Global Equations
parameters.description: Displacement/load control to trace post-buckling paths.

tools.example:
Study 1: Linear Buckling (3 modes)
Definitions > Physics Utilities > Buckling Imperfection: modes 1-2 scaled to 0.1*t
Study 2: Stationary, geometric nonlinearity, auxiliary sweep para = 0..1.2
// Application Library: Structural_Mechanics_Module/Buckling_and_Wrinkling/buckling_corrugated_shell, fuselage_buckling
tools.notes: The imperfection technique is not available for the Layered Shell interface. See the existing Linear Buckling entry.

tools.name: Stress and Strain Variables (Solid Mechanics results)
tools.description: Key predefined result variables of Solid Mechanics (prefix solid., analogous in shell., beam., mbrn., mbd.): displacement magnitude solid.disp, velocity/acceleration solid.vel, solid.acc; Cauchy stress components solid.sxy, second Piola-Kirchhoff solid.SXX and local solid.Sl11; equivalent stresses solid.mises and solid.tresca; principal stresses solid.sp1, solid.sp2, solid.sp3; stress invariants solid.I1s, I2s, I3s, II2s, II3s; strains solid.eXX, local solid.el11, elastic solid.eel11, inelastic solid.eiel11; volume ratio solid.J; equivalent plastic strain solid.epe.
tools.usage: Any result expression, e.g. Surface/Volume plot expr = "solid.mises"; Derived Values > Volume Maximum of solid.mises. Browse Replace Expression > Solid Mechanics > Stress/Strain folders or enable Equation View for the full list.

parameters.name: solid.mises, solid.tresca
parameters.description: von Mises and Tresca equivalent stress.

parameters.name: solid.sp1..sp3
parameters.description: Principal stresses (first = largest).

parameters.name: solid.sxy / solid.SXX / solid.PxX
parameters.description: Cauchy, second and first Piola-Kirchhoff stress components.

parameters.name: solid.eXX, solid.el11, solid.eel11, solid.epe
parameters.description: Green-Lagrange strain, local strain, elastic strain, equivalent plastic strain.

tools.notes: Stresses are evaluated at Gauss points; use Gauss-point evaluation or higher quality settings for accurate peaks. Principal Stress Volume/Surface plots show principal directions (see existing Principal Stress (plot) entry).

tools.name: Reaction Force Variables (Solid Mechanics results)
tools.description: Nodal reaction forces and moments at Dirichlet constraints (Fixed Constraint, Prescribed Displacement, Symmetry...) are available as solid.RFx, solid.RFy, solid.RFz and solid.RMx..RMz; summing them over a boundary with Surface Integration automatically performs a nodal summation. Totals over the interface including spring and damping forces are solid.RFtotalx etc., and per-constraint sums are solid.<tag>.RFsumx (Solid Mechanics and Shell). Reaction moments use a reference point settable in the evaluation.
tools.usage: Results > Derived Values (or Evaluation Group) > Surface Integration of solid.RFz over the constrained boundary; Global Evaluation of solid.RFtotalz or solid.fix1.RFsumz.

parameters.name: solid.RFx, solid.RMx
parameters.description: Nodal reaction force/moment components (not a continuous field).

parameters.name: solid.RFtotalx
parameters.description: Total reaction including spring foundations and dampers.

parameters.name: solid.<tag>.RFsumx
parameters.description: Reaction summed per constraint feature.

parameters.name: solid.Tax / Tracx
parameters.description: Spatial and nominal surface traction for interior or weak evaluations.

tools.notes: Not available for eigenfrequency solutions or weak constraints (use weak-constraint Lagrange multipliers or traction instead) and not for Rigid Material domains (included in totals). Summing separately over adjacent boundaries double-counts shared edge nodes.

tools.name: Energy Variables (Structural Mechanics results)
tools.description: Energy densities and totals defined by the structural interfaces: elastic strain energy density phys.Ws and total phys.Ws_tot (shells split into membrane, bending and shear parts WsM, WsB, WsS), stored energy phys.Wh (frequency domain cycle average), kinetic energy phys.Wk and Wk_tot, and dissipation from plasticity Wp, creep Wc, viscoelasticity Wv, damage Wdmg and phase-field fracture Wfrac with their _tot totals. They are used for energy balance checks, strain-energy-based optimization and energy-based fatigue.
tools.usage: Global Evaluation of solid.Ws_tot, solid.Wk_tot, solid.Wp_tot; volume plots of solid.Ws. Dissipation variables require Calculate dissipated energy / Store dissipation in the material node.

parameters.name: phys.Ws, Ws_tot
parameters.description: Elastic strain energy density (J/m^3) and total (J).

parameters.name: phys.Wk, Wk_tot
parameters.description: Kinetic energy density and total.

parameters.name: phys.Wp, Wc, Wv, Wdmg, Wfrac (+_tot)
parameters.description: Plastic, creep, viscoelastic, damage and fracture dissipation.

parameters.name: phys.Wh, Wh_tot
parameters.description: Cycle-averaged stored energy in frequency domain.

tools.notes: Beams and trusses provide WsL per unit length; the Fatigue Module's energy-based models use dissipated energy per cycle.

tools.name: Beam, Shell and Pipe Datasets (Structural Mechanics results)
tools.description: Structural result templates create special datasets that render lower-dimensional elements with their true extent: the Beam dataset extrudes beam and truss edges with their actual cross sections (showing stresses at section points), the Shell dataset displays shells with thickness and offset and allows evaluation at top, middle or bottom surfaces, and the Pipe dataset renders pipes with their diameter. They are used for realistic 3D stress plots of frames, shells and piping.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Beam | Shell | Pipe (automatically created by default plots). Java: model.result().dataset().create("dset1beam", "Beam"); model.result().dataset().create("dset1shellshl", "Shell").

parameters.name: Source solution dataset
parameters.description: Solution to render.

parameters.name: Evaluation location (Shell)
parameters.description: Relative z position through the thickness (top/mid/bottom).

parameters.name: Cross-section rendering (Beam/Pipe)
parameters.description: Display of true section geometry.

tools.notes: Dataset types Beam, Shell and Pipe were confirmed in library models (default tags such as dset1beam, dset1shellshl, dset1pipem). Layered structures use the Layered Material dataset.
